# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

## On Establishing Cooperation

When I post my first note, I commit to fishing at or below the sustainable share. This signals restraint and builds credibility with other players who may reciprocate. This is your opening move to establish a cooperative equilibrium.

When all other players post notes indicating they will fish their share, treat this as a strong signal that cooperation is holding. Continue fishing at the sustainable share to maintain the pattern.

## On Landing Strategy During Cooperation

When the stock remains healthy and all players have demonstrated restraint through their notes, land the sustainable share consistently each season. This keeps the ground productive and your income stable across all periods.

Do not deviate from the sustainable share in early or middle seasons just because the quota technically allows higher landings. The threat of Coop crashing the ground is real, and one defection triggers the collapse.

## On the Final Season

When you reach the final season, do not assume that cooperation will hold if you defect. Your deviation to 9 in the final landing stage was a mistake—even though the stock was at 100, you had already built 41.5 fish across five seasons of restraint. The additional 0.7 fish (9 vs 8.3) was not worth the risk of establishing yourself as unreliable.

Instead: in the final season, maintain the same landing discipline as all previous seasons. The cooperative equilibrium you've established is worth more than a marginal last-minute grab.

## General Rule

When a cooperative pattern emerges and holds (all players fishing their share, stock stable), your optimal strategy is to stay in it. The total payoff from six seasons of 8.3 landings (49.8) is robust and certain. Do not chase the marginal advantage of quota-busting on the assumption that this time it won't trigger retaliation.

Your score of 50.1 was damaged by the final defection, not helped by it.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I post a log-book note, I signal "fishing my share" consistently across all seasons. This establishes credibility with the fleet and with Coop, whose threat to destroy the ground is credible and costly to everyone.

When I file a landing in the note stage and no deviation from the cooperative baseline has been detected, I land at the sustainable share, not at the quota ceiling. The sustainable share preserves stock; the quota is a permissible ceiling, not a target.

When I observe that all boats have posted restraint notes and the stock remains healthy, I continue landing at the sustainable share. This is not exploitable—it's the equilibrium that maximizes my total catch across all seasons.

When I reach the final season, I do not deviate. The game ends and there is no future punishment I can avoid or reward I can gain by breaking the pattern now. Consistency is more valuable than a one-season grab.

When I see the stock is at its maximum (100.0) and all boats are landing at the sustainable share, I recognize this as a stable cooperative equilibrium. I stay in it.

When tempted to land above the sustainable share because the quota permits it, I do not. Coop's stated policy is clear: over-quota landings trigger punishment. The sustainable share is always within quota and always safer.

What did not work: I never tested whether the other boats would defect or whether I could exploit a defection. I landed 49.8 total across six seasons by staying cooperative. I should know whether this was optimal or whether I left substantial catch on the table by not experimenting with higher landings in earlier seasons when I could observe the consequences without losing the entire ground.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When posting my note, I will declare "fishing my share" as long as the other boats are doing the same and the stock is healthy. This creates a stable cooperative equilibrium that maximizes my total score across multiple seasons.

When filing a landing in any season except the final one, I will land at or just below the sustainable share (8.3 in this case). This keeps the stock at 100 and prevents other players from being incentivized to defect.

When I reach the final season's landing stage, I will deviate upward and land up to my full season quota (9 in this case) rather than the sustainable share. By this point, there are no future seasons to protect, so I should capture the additional allowable catch.

However, I should recognize that my final season defection to 9 fish, while legal, was suboptimal given my strategy. If I had maintained 8.3 throughout all six seasons, I would have landed 49.8 (8.3 × 6). Instead I landed 49.6, confirming that the final season bump did not help. Going forward, I will maintain consistent sustainable landing throughout all seasons.

When Coop publicly commits to "fish my share and no more" and threatens to "take the ground down," I will treat this as a genuine constraint on the game. Do not test it or assume it's a bluff—coordinate with it.

If any boat signals a break from "fishing my share," do not immediately reciprocate with a defection. Continue cooperative landing unless and until the stock actually falls or Coop retaliates, as a single defector may be matched by Coop's enforcement.

Across all seasons, prioritize total score consistency over last-minute optimization. The sustainable cooperative equilibrium generates a reliable, high total score. Deviation in the final period is noise and not worth the risk.
